frozen_decisions_applied: Plan S5 #16: 'Preserve eFuse/security state, flash/NVS encryption key material, factory GatewayId source, manufacturing PoP, product CA/trust anchors and encrypted device TLS current/next slots.' -- the classification itself was already complete (Section 2.7, plan #15); this sub-slice adds the enforcement that makes it structural: erase_namespace()/erase_namespace_key_range() refuse outright, before touching any key, any namespace not classified kEraseOnFactoryReset.

Plan S5 #17: 'Mark admin/session, Wi-Fi, MQTT, Zigbee network/device/reporting, Matter, operation journal and legacy migration/tombstone data for erase. Provide typed namespace erase operations; do not use broad whole-partition erase that can touch preserved material.' -- implemented as two typed functions built directly on Section 2.10's secure_storage_erase, both sharing the same structural refusal guarantee.

This project's established real-tool-grounding discipline caught a real, previously-unnoticed target-specific bug: erase_namespace_key_range()'s dynamic key formatting used a bare %02u against a uint32_t argument, which compiles correctly on the x86-64 host toolchain (uint32_t == unsigned int there) but mismatches on the real ESP32-C6 riscv32 target (uint32_t == unsigned long there) -- caught only by the real idf.py build, fixed with an explicit static_cast<unsigned>(), matching hal_nvs.c's own established cast convention for exactly this class of issue.

erase_namespace_implemented.detail: erase_namespace(namespace_id) refuses (kRefusedNotErasable) any namespace whose Section 2.7 registry classification is not kEraseOnFactoryReset, before calling secure_storage_erase for anything. For an erasable namespace, iterates every EXACT (non-prefix) key pattern and erases each via secure_storage_erase, folding results into kErased/kPartialFailure. Deliberately does NOT expand prefix key patterns -- documented directly as a named limitation, not hidden.

erase_namespace_key_range_implemented.detail: erase_namespace_key_range(namespace_id, prefix, suffix_chars, suffix_char_count, index_count) handles the one real prefix-pattern case in this codebase (kZigbeeNetworkDeviceReporting's dynamically-built per-reporting-profile keys), building '<prefix><suffix_char><2-digit index>' for every combination and erasing each -- matching config_manager.cpp's real build_profile_nvs_key/build_legacy_v2_profile_nvs_key key format exactly, not a guessed shape. Same structural refusal guarantee as erase_namespace(). Rejects null prefix/suffix_chars defensively.

real_bug_found_and_fixed.status: COMPLETE -- found by the real ESP-IDF target build, not the host build
real_bug_found_and_fixed.detail: erase_namespace_key_range()'s std::snprintf call originally used '%02u' against the loop's uint32_t index variable. On the x86-64 host toolchain (zgw-host-tools:s0), uint32_t resolves to unsigned int, exactly matching %u, so the host build and all host tests passed cleanly with no warning. Compiling for the real ESP32-C6 riscv32 target inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5 failed with -Werror on a format-specifier mismatch, because that toolchain's uint32_t resolves to unsigned long instead. Fixed with an explicit static_cast<unsigned>(index), matching hal_nvs.c's own pre-existing (unsigned) casts in its own %u log format strings (the same reasoning already established there). Verified by a second, clean full real-target build after the fix (1186/1186 steps, vs. the failing attempt's partial 1148/1186 before the fix).

tests_and_verification.detail: 7 tests in test/host/test_factory_reset_namespace_erase.cpp, all passing: a PRESERVE-classified namespace (kTlsIdentity) is refused and its data proven untouched; kResetJournal (RESET_JOURNAL_ONLY) is refused the same way, the first concrete proof of plan #18's 'survives erasing' property; an ERASE-classified namespace's exact keys are actually erased; a namespace with both exact and prefix keys has only its exact keys cleared by erase_namespace() (proving the documented limitation, not just asserting it); erase_namespace_key_range() clears the real rptp_/reporting-profile shape (suffix_chars='dcirk', index_count=16, matching ConfigManager::kMaxReportingProfiles); the range function refuses a PRESERVE-classified namespace; null prefix/suffix_chars are rejected. deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: erase_namespace() erases only exact key patterns; prefix-pattern namespaces need the separate erase_namespace_key_range() call, and the registry itself provides no automatic way to discover the correct range parameters for a given prefix (a caller must know them, as this sub-slice's own tests do for the one real case).
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The Section 2.7 registry only stores prefix strings, not the real bounded keyspace a specific owning module (e.g. config_manager.cpp, which alone knows ConfigManager::kMaxReportingProfiles and the exact suffix-character set) builds from them -- a generic mechanism would require either a HAL-level NVS key-enumeration primitive that does not exist, or duplicating that owning-module knowledge into the registry itself, both larger changes than this sub-slice's scope.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A future real reset flow (S8) erasing kZigbeeNetworkDeviceReporting completely needs to call both erase_namespace() (for the exact keys) AND erase_namespace_key_range() (for each real prefix, with the correct parameters) explicitly -- there is no single call that does both automatically for a namespace with mixed exact/prefix keys.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Nothing in this repository calls either erase_namespace() or erase_namespace_key_range() -- this is pure scaffolding, matching every S5 sub-slice's discipline.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: The real factory-reset flow that would drive these functions is S8's job, built on top of this stage's foundation, not S5's.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: No production behavior changes as a result of this sub-slice; the functions exist, are tested, and are ready for S8 to consume.
